Dedicated assistant and business operations

Define how an executive virtual assistant fits your coverage, tools and decision rules. Use one work log for the executive, assistant and backup owner.

Executive communications and records

An email management virtual assistant can triage mail and voicemail, draft correspondence and prepare a daily brief. The same queue can include proofreading, transcription and contact or task records.

Meetings, travel and expenses

A calendar management virtual assistant can prepare agendas, take notes and coordinate approved flights, hotels and ground transport. Organise receipts, reimbursement inputs and itineraries for review.

Projects, vendors and events

An administrative virtual assistant can track owners, deadlines and standard procedures, research suppliers, coordinate quote and purchase order follow-ups, and maintain guest lists and venue logistics.

Board and client coordination

Collect pre-reads and draft slide decks, track board actions and investor follow-ups, and organise client onboarding, status updates and reports. The owner approves commitments and distribution.

Personal and lifestyle coordination

Agree a separate scope for personal logistics and the permissions it needs. The administrative virtual assistant can prepare options and coordinate approved arrangements around your working schedule.

Family and household logistics

Coordinate family calendars, school and activity schedules, household providers, maintenance, pet appointments, moves and relocation. Research gifts, arrange approved purchases or shipping and track errands.

Personal travel and events

Compare family travel options, prepare reservations and itineraries, and coordinate gatherings, restaurants, guest communications and vendor follow-ups. Confirm spending and cancellation rules first.

Wellbeing administration

Coordinate appointment and referral research, bookings, insurance reimbursements and follow-ups. At your request, organise records, refill reminders, fitness and meal logistics, wellness bookings or personal tracking records within agreed privacy rules. Clinical decisions stay with you and your care team.

Where your executive virtual assistant helps

An email management virtual assistant works from approved examples. A calendar management virtual assistant also needs the rules for conflicts, rescheduling and time zones.

Your inbox gets ahead of you.

A morning brief groups messages into decisions, drafts and items to watch. Priority contacts are flagged using rules you set.

Every meeting creates loose ends.

An action register records what was agreed, who owns it and when a follow-up is due.

The week keeps reshuffling.

Calendar changes come with a short note about what moved, what conflicts and what still needs confirmation.

What to verify before closing a task.

An email management virtual assistant needs clear reply limits. A calendar management virtual assistant needs a named approver for changes affecting other commitments.

  • Confirm time zone, invitees and meeting links.
  • Flag anything that requires a response in your voice.
  • Record changes that affect another person’s calendar.
  • Review open actions before the weekly handoff.

Read about trust and access

A morning brief that earns its place

Your executive virtual assistant can collect the day’s unresolved choices. An email management virtual assistant should keep routine replies separate from those decisions.

An executive shares an inbox and calendar with an administrative virtual assistant for a sample two-week pilot. The first goal is a reliable morning brief that separates decisions from information. The pilot also needs to protect private appointments and prevent conflicting instructions from two people who use the same calendar.

  1. 01

    Read the inbox against the calendar

    At the start of the agreed window, check new messages for a deadline or a change to an event. Link the original email to the calendar item. Put changes that affect travel time or another participant in the decision list, even when the new time itself is available.

  2. 02

    Make decisions easy to find

    Put the time-sensitive items first. Write the action the executive needs to take, give the relevant deadline, and link to the source. Keep drafted replies and ordinary reminders in their own groups so a reader can scan the brief without opening every thread.

  3. 03

    Close the day with a record

    Record the decisions made, which invitations changed, and what still needs a reply. Keep open actions in one place rather than copying a running list into every email. At the next review, confirm what should move to the following day.

Prepare the inputs and rules.

Give your administrative virtual assistant one normal request and one exception. Your calendar management virtual assistant can use both to check the scheduling rules.

Priority contacts

List the people and organisations that should always be flagged. For each, agree whether a message should go straight to the executive or into the next brief. A title alone is rarely enough to determine urgency.

Calendar preferences

Write down working hours, time zones, buffers and protected blocks. Give two examples of meetings that may be moved and one that requires approval even if it looks routine.

Sending authority

Use separate rules for drafting, sending and changing an invitation. Confirm which mailbox or alias each rule applies to and where to record when a message has been approved.

Decide what happens when the normal rule fails.

Your executive virtual assistant should record why a request is blocked. An email management virtual assistant can draft a reply while waiting for the owner.

Conflicting instructions

Two organisers ask for the same protected slot. Note the conflict, show the alternatives and ask the calendar owner to choose before accepting either request.

A message contains a sensitive decision

Move the decision to the agreed private channel. Keep the general work log to the minimum needed to show that it is awaiting review.

A deadline is unclear

Check the source and time zone first. If there is still a gap, flag the assumption and suggest the safest next step before moving another person’s meeting.

Review your calendar management virtual assistant’s work

Review the brief with your administrative virtual assistant. Compare how your calendar management virtual assistant handled a normal appointment and a last-minute conflict.

Decision quality

Look at three items escalated during the week. Check whether each gave the executive enough context to act and whether a routine item could have been handled under a clearer rule.

Scheduling accuracy

Compare a sample of invites with the source messages. Confirm the attendee list, time zone, meeting location and any buffer that was promised.

Open action age

Review actions that rolled over more than once. Decide whether the owner is wrong, the deadline changed or the executive needs to intervene.

Leave a record the next person can use.

Your executive virtual assistant needs a record another person can follow. Your administrative virtual assistant should keep the latest instructions beside open requests.

Part of the handoverWhat to recordWhat the next owner can do
Current workWhat to recordInclude the latest version, the source link and the current status. Note what was already checked and which changes were approved.What the next owner can doContinue from the latest approved state without searching for the source or repeating a completed check.
Open decisionsWhat to recordList each outstanding decision, the person who can make it and the point at which the next owner should follow up.What the next owner can doPrioritise the blocked items and ask a specific question when the next approval is due.
Time-sensitive commitmentsWhat to recordState the time zone, the next update due and any commitments that someone has already shared. Include the agreed backup contact.What the next owner can doKeep the next promise visible and make sure requests that cannot wait reach the correct person.
Changes to the instructionsWhat to recordRecord which rule changed, who approved it and when it starts. Keep an example that shows the difference in practice.What the next owner can doUse the current rule and compare new work with the agreed example during the next review.

Plan calendar management virtual assistant coverage

Agree the review windows for your email management virtual assistant. A calendar management virtual assistant may need a different check during travel or deadline weeks.

Ordinary days

Choose one time for the inbox brief and agree when it needs a second pass. A morning brief might cover changes for the next day and outstanding replies, with a later check reserved for meetings that can no longer wait.

Travel or deadline weeks

Share the dates, time zones and people who can approve changes. Ask for a separate list of flight changes, rescheduling requests and meeting conflicts so routine messages stay out of the urgent queue.

When the executive is unavailable

Give the administrative virtual assistant a backup for each decision type, such as the meeting owner for a reschedule or the finance lead for a booking change. Record how long to wait before escalating and what can safely be drafted while waiting.

Frequently Asked Questions

Before choosing an administrative virtual assistant, agree the tools and coverage. Ask which decisions your executive virtual assistant should send back to you.

Can an administrative virtual assistant reply from my inbox?

Decide which routine replies can be sent using approved wording, and which should be drafted for you.

What should I hand over first?

A recurring task with a clear output works well. Try a daily inbox and calendar brief with a short list of priority contacts.

How are calendar conflicts handled?

Give the administrative virtual assistant rules for which meetings can move, how much notice to give and who decides when priorities conflict.

Can you prepare meetings and track the actions afterward?

Agree which meetings need an agenda and what the action record should include. Give each follow-up an owner and due date.

What belongs in an executive brief?

Include upcoming commitments, items that need a decision, and actions that are waiting on another person. Agree how urgent items should reach you.

Can you support more than one executive?

Scope the inboxes, calendars, priority rules and coverage for each person. Agree who resolves conflicts between competing requests.
